subject.title: fix: tighten control ui input validation [AI]

question: Should OpenClaw deliberately reject .atom repository previews and truncate assistant-media filenames above 200 code points, or preserve those inputs unless a documented upstream or header limit requires rejection?
rationale: Both choices are plausible hardening policies, but they intentionally narrow behavior introduced by a recent merged Control UI change and the available evidence does not establish the permanent compatibility contract.

options.title: Prove and narrow limits
options.body: Verify GitHub’s reserved repository suffixes and the actual safe Content-Disposition byte budget, then reject or truncate only inputs outside those contracts.

options.title: Accept stricter policy
options.body: Confirm the .atom rejection and 200-code-point cap as intentional compatibility changes and require explicit release and upgrade evidence before merge.

recommendation.title: Prove and narrow limits
recommendation.body: Verify GitHub’s reserved repository suffixes and the actual safe Content-Disposition byte budget, then reject or truncate only inputs outside those contracts.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the current filename-preservation behavior and is best positioned to decide whether the new bounded policy matches that owner contract.
